title: Specrun run record
description: Schema for run.json, the file in a run's directory (runs/<run ID>/ under specrun's log directory) that says what the run was. Written by specrun when the run starts, and again when it ends, then with ended_at and envelope. Never written by hand.

run_id.description: The run's ID, which is also the name of its directory: the UTC time the run started, to the second, then the milliseconds as three digits and one hex digit drawn at random.

started_at.description: When the run started, RFC 3339 in UTC, to the second.

ended_at.description: When the run ended, RFC 3339 in UTC, to the second. Absent while the run is going, and for good on a run that never ended, as after a crash, a kill or a reboot.

pid.description: The process ID of the specrun that made the run.

settings.description: The settings the run ran with, each flag as its environment variable and its default resolved it.

max.description: --max: the packages the run may land; 0 is no limit.

stall.description: --stall: how long a session may write nothing before it counts as stalled, as a Go duration (30m0s).

log_dir.description: The log directory as it resolved, an absolute path: the directory that holds ledger.jsonl and runs/.

reconcile_every.description: --reconcile-every: the landed packages after which a reconcile runs; 0 leaves only the reconcile at the end.

stop_on.description: --stop-on: the severities of an open defect that stop the loop after the package that opened it; empty stops on none.

repair.description: --repair: whether the run repairs each open defect of a severity in stop_on that a landed package left, instead of stopping.

repair_on.description: --repair-on: what a reconcile queues for repair, defects by severity and untested items; empty queues nothing.

repair_max.description: --repair-max: the most repairs after one reconcile; 0 repairs nothing there.

repair_security.description: --repair-security: whether security defects are repaired too; without it one never is.

strict_skills.description: --strict-skills: whether an af-impl skill other than the one specrun was built with refuses the run.

strict_handoffs.description: --strict-handoffs: whether a package that leaves an inbound handoff untaken is refused.

versions.description: What the run ran. Absent when the run stopped before it found them.

skill_path.description: The af-impl SKILL.md a session in the repository loads: the project's own copy before the user's.

skill_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of that file in hex, or the words not installed.

built_skill_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the af-impl skill specrun was built with, in hex, or the word unknown.

claude.description: What the claude command gives as its version.

issue.description: What the issue command gives as its version.

envelope.description: The envelope the run wrote to stdout, whole. This schema names the fields every command's envelope has; result is specrun's own (see the envelope section of docs/specrun.md), and neither it nor the other fields are constrained here.

ok.description: True only when the run did the whole job it was asked to do.

status.description: The outcome in words, from exit_code.

exit_code.description: The process exit code: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 usage error.

error.description: What failed and where; present exactly when ok is false.

result.description: What the run did: what landed, where it stopped, the diagnosis, the run's ID and directory.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock time of the run, in milliseconds.

started_at.description: When the run started, RFC 3339 in UTC.
